To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the enzymes involved in glucose-6-phosphate metabolism in brain are functionally cytosolic; the activities of these enzymes do not vary significantly in extracts from different areas of brain; the NADPH/NADP ratio controls the operation of glucose metabolism in brain; and UDPG pyrophos- phorylase is not present in an inactive form.

the enzymes of the glycolytic and pentose phosphate pathways are mainly cytoplasmic in brain, that the pentose pathway is controlled by the NADPH/NADP ratio and that glycogen synthetase is mainly in the glucose dependent form and glycogem phosphorylase mainly as b enzyme.

the glucose 6- phosphate metabolic crossroads in the brain, i.e., the pentose cycle and glycogen synthetase and phosphorylase, are under the control of the NADPH/NADP ratio, that the UDPG pyrophosphate pathway is not an active route of glucose utilization, and that glucose 6-phosphatase is not an important enzyme of brain tissue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the metabolism of glucose 6- phosphate in brain.
the elucidation of the mechanisms of regulation of glucose 6- phosphate metabolism in brain.
the study of the enzymes involved in the metabolism of glucose 6- phosphate in brain tissue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
glucose 6-phosphae is metabolized in the brain by the glycopolytic pathway and by the pentose cycle, and that the operation of the latter is mainly controlled by the NADPH/NADP ratio.

glucose 6-phosphates are metabolized in the cytoplasm of brain cells by glycolysis and pentose phosphate pathways and by glycogen synthesis and degradation, but the operation of the last two pathways is limited by the availability of glucose 6 phosphate.
the glucose 6 phosphate metabolic crossroads in the brain is the site of regulation of glucose utilization in the brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
glucose 6-phosphatase is the key enzyme in the glucose 5-phosphate metabolic cross-roads in brain.
the pentose phosphate cycle in brain is a metabolic pathway of minor importance.
the brain is not a tissue in which a large part of its glucose is metabolized by the pentose cycle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain is a glucose-dependent organ and it is not a good idea to deprive it of glucose for long periods of time.
glucose-6-phosphate is a metabolic crossroads for brain.
the enzymes involved in glucose metabolism in the brain are cytoplasmic and that the operation of the glucose 6phosphate metabolic crossroads is mainly controlled by the NADPH/NADP ratio.
